umbrella_banners.note: IFRS statements print EQUITY AND LIABILITIES above the Equity, Non-current and Current sub-banners; reading it as equity would refuse every liability line item beneath it.
Schedule III prints ASSETS as an umbrella over the Non-Current and Current sub-banners. Reading it as a section of its own would scope every asset line to a section no concept declares.

exclusive_vocabularies.note: IAS 7 divides cash flows into exactly three activities and a statement labels each subtotal with its own, so naming one rules out the others.

normalisation.note: Applied to every candidate row label and every alias before comparison. The quoted literals in each step are that step's own vocabulary — `row_reconstruct._quoted_examples` harvests them — so they are configuration, not illustration.
pipeline: Full-width to half-width punctuation; map ╱ ／ ⁄ to /; map （） to ().

Strip footnote and note markers: trailing digits in parentheses, superscripts, '(note 12)', '(Refer note 36)', '(Refer Note 2A)', and the asterisk, caret, hash and dagger an Indian filing hangs off a caption to key it to a sub-note: '*', '^', '#', '†'.
Strip leading numbering and bullets: '1.', '(a)', '(i)', 'A.', '-'. Schedule III numbers its own sub-captions this way.
Strip trailing colons and dashes used to introduce sub-captions ('Trade Payables:', 'Total Outstanding dues of -').

Strip inline unit and currency annotations: '(₹ in Crores)', '(₹ in Lakhs)', '(` in Crores)', '(` in crores)', 'Rs. in crores', 'Rs. in lakhs', 'INR in million', '₹', '(unaudited)', '(Audited)'. THE GRAVE ACCENT IS NOT A TYPO: an Indian PDF whose font lacks the ₹ glyph substitutes ` for it, and both forms occur in one document.
Collapse internal whitespace to a single space; strip zero-width characters and soft hyphens.
Join a wrapped caption to its continuation line before matching, then also retain the bare fragment as a fallback candidate.
normalisation.wrapped_caption_rule:
A Schedule III statement prints a mandatory 'Note No.' column BETWEEN the caption and the figures, and its captions are long enough to wrap in the width that leaves: 'Total Outstanding dues of creditors other than Micro Enterprises' / 'and Small Enterprises' is one caption on two physical lines, and read as two it matches neither. Reassemble from the value row upward before matching; match the reassembled string first, and use the bare fragment only if that fails.

THE NOTE COLUMN IS NOT A FIGURE. That same mandatory column is numeric and sits left of the amounts, so its value is the first number on the row and reads as the current period unless it is removed. Resolve it geometrically where the column can be located and by shape otherwise — a bare one- or two-digit integer, optionally suffixed A or B ('2A', '4B', '11A'), followed on the row by a real amount.

binding.note: Precedence is section-first. A concept can only claim a row printed inside one of its section_scope values.
order: 1. Resolve the statement (balance_sheet / profit_and_loss / cash_flow) from the page or table caption.

2. Resolve the printed section from the nearest preceding section header. If no header is resolvable, the row is unbound: route to review, never guess a section. (A row WITH a resolved section that no concept claims is not unbound — it is swept into that section's residual; see unbound_row_policy.)
3. Restrict the candidate concept set to concepts whose section_scope contains the resolved section.
4. Rule tier: exact normalised alias, then regex_hints, in descending match_priority. Any exclude_hints hit is a hard veto, not a score penalty.
5. Semantic tier over the restricted set only, using definition + include + exclude. Never over the full ontology.
6. Tie between concepts listed in each other's confusable_with: resolve with section_disambiguation; if still tied, emit both as candidates and route to review. Never pick by declaration order.
7. Residual sweep (see residual_framework) runs last, over rows no dedicated concept claimed.
8. Reconcile the section against its reported subtotal.
binding.unbound_row_policy: Route an unclaimed face value only to the residual for its resolved printed section. Never borrow a neighbouring concept or cross a section. After all mapping and gap-closing opportunities, the engine-level face_mapping_contract gives any remaining face value a unique engine_unclassified_face key outside the ontology/template namespaces. This keeps the row stored and reviewable without feeding it into an unrelated calculation. Verified non-additive aggregates replaced by mapped components remain evidence-only.
binding.match_priority: Integer 0-99, higher evaluated first. Long specific captions rank above short generic ones so 'Total assets less current liabilities' cannot be pre-empted by 'Total current liabilities' on token overlap. Residuals are 0 and unreachable by matching.

prompt: Map each line item basis their definition, additional information provided and exclusion criteria. Rely on financial meaning and not just words - these are Ind AS financial statements of Indian entities, presented under Schedule III, Division II of the Companies Act 2013. Amounts are in INR and are usually scaled in lakhs or crores. Expect Schedule III wording: Other Equity rather than reserves, Trade Payables split between micro and small enterprises and others, Financial Assets and Financial Liabilities as presentation groups, Property Plant and Equipment with Capital work-in-progress, and Revenue from operations separate from Other income.

sign_convention.stored_value: The reported value after paren-to-negative conversion.
sign_convention.expenses_and_outflows: Stored NEGATIVE. This is required by the template: pl_gross_profit = sum(revenue, cost_of_goods_sold) and pl_profit_before_exceptional_items_and_tax = sum(total_income, total_operating_cost, total_non_operating_expense) only hold if expense concepts carry a negative sign.
sign_convention.unsigned_source: Where a filing prints expenses as unsigned positives in a by-nature list, negate on load and set sign_normalised: true on the fact so the transformation is auditable.
sign_convention.either: Subtotals, working-capital movements, fair-value changes, share of results, OCI and net cash flows are sign-indeterminate. Retain the reported sign; never coerce.
sign_convention.validation: A concept whose sign_convention is positive_expected or negative_expected but whose loaded value carries the opposite sign is a review trigger, not an auto-correction.

global_rules.face_only_default: Concepts default to face_only: true. Notes are evidence for a face amount, never an independent source of one, unless note_use is decomposition_allowed.
global_rules.duplicate_fact_rule: The same economic fact on the face and in a note is one fact with multiple evidence references, not two additive values. This also applies to two face captions that report the same amount (see equivalence blocks).
parent_child_allocation: Never load a gross parent and its separately mapped children additively.
Residual = reported parent minus confirmed included children.
Subtract only on explicit inclusion wording, hierarchy, reconciliation or arithmetic support.
If containment is uncertain, retain the parent as evidence and route to review.
global_rules.no_fabricated_split: Never invent a decomposition. Where only a combined figure is reported, load the combined concept and leave the children empty. The one exception is a concept declaring sole_component_of: assigning a whole undifferentiated figure to a single child divides nothing, and it is refused as soon as any sibling child is evidenced on the face or in the subtotal's own note.
global_rules.totals_policy: Compute totals from mutually exclusive concept outputs. Use reported totals only for validation, never as an input to the components.

scope_selection.note: An Indian annual report presents the STANDALONE and the CONSOLIDATED financial statements in full, one after the other, in the same document — so the entity has to be resolved for two complete sets of statements, not for two columns of one.

entity_scope.rule: Resolve the entity from the statement's own title and column headings, never from position. An Indian filing titles them 'Balance Sheet' / 'Consolidated Balance Sheet' and 'Statement of Profit and Loss' / 'Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss'; the standalone set is usually printed first and the consolidated set after it, but neither order is universal. Record entity_scope on every fact and never mix the two sets within one statement.
company_only_markers: Presence of bs_nca__investment_in_subsidiaries on the face is strong evidence the statement is STANDALONE, since consolidation eliminates it. An Indian standalone balance sheet prints 'Investments in Subsidiaries and Associates' as its own non-current caption, which the consolidated one replaces with 'Investments in Associates and Joint Ventures' accounted for under the equity method.

period_selection.rule: The Indian financial year ends 31 March, and columns are headed 'As at 31.03.2026' / 'As at 31st March 2026' on the balance sheet and 'Year 2025-26' or 'For the year ended 31st March 2026' on the profit and loss. Identify the current period from the heading date rather than from column position, and load comparatives only into the comparative slot.
period_selection.restatement_rule: Where a comparative is labelled restated, or reopened by a scheme of amalgamation or arrangement ('Restated balance as at 1st April 2024', 'Changes on account of amalgamation'), load it as the comparative and set restated: true. Keep both figures with the flag rather than overwriting an original comparative already loaded — a court- or NCLT-approved scheme routinely restates the opening balance sheet.

units_and_currency.rule: Resolve currency and scale from the statement header, not the cover page, and re-resolve per statement — an Indian report commonly states the financial statements in crores and a subsidiary schedule or a BRSR table in lakhs or absolute rupees. Persist unit on every fact; never normalise scale silently. 1 crore = 10 million = 100 lakh.
units_and_currency.conflict: If the header scale and a printed subtotal are inconsistent by a factor of 100 or 1,000, trust neither and route the statement to review. The factor of 100 is the one to watch on an Indian filing, because it is the lakh-to-crore step and a mis-read there is not an order of magnitude but two.

scope_selection.column_guard: Every fact carries the resolved (entity_scope, period, currency, unit). Two facts for the same canonical_key that differ on any of these are distinct facts, not duplicates — which is what keeps the standalone and the consolidated set of the same filing from colliding.

residual_framework.note: One definition governing the 11 output-template subsection residuals. Each uses an existing template line; no template row is added.

sweep.runs: after all dedicated concepts in the section have been resolved, before section reconciliation
sweep.candidate_set: every printed value row on the FACE of the statement whose resolved section equals the residual's single section_scope value
eligibility: The row printed a value for the selected entity_scope, period, currency and unit.
No dedicated concept whose section_scope contains this section claimed the row.

The row is not a section subtotal, statement total, section header, attribution caption, per-share figure, narrative row, note-reference-only row, truncated caption, an "of which" breakdown of the row above it or a sub-enumerated component of it ((a)… or 1.… beneath a numbered head) — each of those amounts is already inside the row above, so sweeping it counts the same money twice.
The row was printed INSIDE this section. A row printed in any other section is ineligible however similar its wording — there is no cross-section rescue.

The row's sign agrees with the section's sign_convention, where the section states one. A row signed against its section is evidence the SECTION is wrong, not the amount, so it goes to review rather than into the bucket — a cost swept into income moves the income subtotal and every total below it.
sweep.plug_behaviour: forbidden — the residual is never computed as (reported subtotal − mapped children)
sweep.literal_others_caption: A row captioned 'Others' or 'Miscellaneous' is simply one unmapped face row and sweeps in as a single component. It gets no privileged treatment and no dedicated concept.

itemisation.rule: The residual's value is the arithmetic sum of its components. Original labels and signs are always retained; a swept row is never relabelled to 'Others'.

reconciliation.identity: reported_section_subtotal − Σ(dedicated concepts in section) − Σ(residual components) = 0
reconciliation.tolerance: one rounding unit per contributing row
reconciliation.on_failure: Emit an unallocated_gap fact carrying the difference and route the section to review. Never adjust the residual, and never adjust a dedicated concept, to close the gap.
reconciliation.sections_without_reported_subtotal: If the section prints no subtotal, the residual is still itemised but is flagged unreconciled and carries lower confidence.

review_triggers: any single component exceeds 2% of |reported section subtotal|
a component label scored at or above the semantic threshold against a dedicated concept but was vetoed by exclude_hints
residual sign is opposite to the section's sign_convention
the section reconciliation emitted an unallocated_gap
prohibitions: Never populated by alias, regex or embedding match.
Never carries a value with no itemised components.
Never absorbs a row a dedicated concept could have claimed but was not tested for — all dedicated concepts in the section must be evaluated first.
Never spans sections, statements, periods, entity scopes or units.

items.label: Land
items.definition: Freehold land the entity owns and holds for its own use, where the balance sheet prints it as a row of its own among the non-current assets ('Land', 'Freehold land'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Gross Fixed Assets, beside Buildings, Leasehold Improvements, Plant & Equipment, Furniture & Fixtures, Vehicles & Transport Equipment, Other Fixed Assets and Construction in Progress. Take the class at the amount the balance sheet carries it: net of accumulated depreciation and impairment, as an Ind AS balance sheet prints property, plant and equipment; at cost only where the face itself prints the class at cost with the accumulated depreciation as a separate deduction row, which is then 'Accum Deprec & Impairment(-)'. Not this line: leasehold land and other land held under a lease, which Ind AS 116 carries in right-of-use assets (the Schedule III row 'Right-of-use assets', which this template places on 'Land use rights'); land and buildings printed together ('Buildings'); land held as investment property ('Investment Property(Net)'); land held for development or sale, which is inventory. Schedule III prints 'Property, Plant and Equipment' as one row: that row is 'Plant & Equipment' as printed and is not split into classes from the reconciliation of its carrying amount by class, so this line then has no row of its own. Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list.

items.label: Buildings
items.definition: Buildings held for the entity's own use — offices, factories, warehouses — including land and buildings printed together, where the balance sheet prints them as a row of their own among the non-current assets ('Buildings', 'Land and buildings', 'Leasehold land and buildings'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Gross Fixed Assets, beside Land, Leasehold Improvements, Plant & Equipment, Furniture & Fixtures, Vehicles & Transport Equipment, Other Fixed Assets and Construction in Progress. Take the class at the amount the balance sheet carries it: net of accumulated depreciation and impairment, as an Ind AS balance sheet prints property, plant and equipment; at cost only where the face itself prints the class at cost with the accumulated depreciation as a separate deduction row, which is then 'Accum Deprec & Impairment(-)'. Not this line: buildings held to earn rentals or for capital appreciation ('Investment Property(Net)'); buildings under construction, which Schedule III prints as 'Capital work-in-progress' ('Construction in Progress'); leased premises carried as right-of-use assets ('Land use rights', where this template places the 'Right-of-use assets' row); properties held for sale, which are inventory or 'Assets Related to Disc Ops'. Schedule III prints 'Property, Plant and Equipment' as one row: that row is 'Plant & Equipment' as printed and is not split into classes from the reconciliation of its carrying amount by class, so this line then has no row of its own. Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list.

items.label: Leasehold Improvements
items.definition: Improvements, fit-out and renovation the entity has made to premises it leases, and land improvements, carried as a class of fixed assets in a row of its own among the non-current assets of the balance sheet ('Leasehold improvements', 'Improvements to leasehold premises', 'Land improvements'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Gross Fixed Assets, beside Land, Buildings, Plant & Equipment, Furniture & Fixtures, Vehicles & Transport Equipment, Other Fixed Assets and Construction in Progress. Take the class at the amount the balance sheet carries it: net of accumulated depreciation and impairment, as an Ind AS balance sheet prints property, plant and equipment; at cost only where the face itself prints the class at cost with the accumulated depreciation as a separate deduction row, which is then 'Accum Deprec & Impairment(-)'. Not this line: buildings ('Buildings'); the leased premises themselves, carried as right-of-use assets ('Land use rights', where this template places the 'Right-of-use assets' row); capital advances paid for such work ('Other Non-Current Assets'). Schedule III prints 'Property, Plant and Equipment' as one row: that row is 'Plant & Equipment' as printed and is not split into classes from the reconciliation of its carrying amount by class, so this line then has no row of its own. Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list.

items.label: Plant & Equipment
items.definition: Plant, machinery and equipment held for use in production, supply or administration — plant and machinery, computers, office and electrical equipment — and, because Schedule III prints property, plant and equipment as a single row among the non-current assets, that whole row as printed ('Property, Plant and Equipment', 'Property, plant and equipment', 'Tangible assets'). That single row is cited as it stands and not split into Land, Buildings, Furniture & Fixtures or the other classes from the reconciliation of its carrying amount by class; those lines then answer empty. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Gross Fixed Assets, beside Land, Buildings, Leasehold Improvements, Furniture & Fixtures, Vehicles & Transport Equipment, Other Fixed Assets and Construction in Progress. Take the row at the amount the balance sheet carries it: net of accumulated depreciation and impairment, as an Ind AS balance sheet prints it; at cost only where the face itself prints it at cost with the accumulated depreciation as a separate deduction row, which is then 'Accum Deprec & Impairment(-)'. Not this line: 'Capital work-in-progress' ('Construction in Progress'); 'Right-of-use assets' (placed by this template on 'Land use rights'); 'Investment Property' ('Investment Property(Net)'); bearer plants and biological assets other than bearer plants printed as rows of their own ('Other Fixed Assets'); intangible assets. Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list.

items.label: Furniture & Fixtures
items.definition: Furniture, fixtures and fittings held for the entity's own use, as a class of fixed assets printed in a row of its own among the non-current assets of the balance sheet ('Furniture and fixtures', 'Furniture and fittings', 'Fixtures'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Gross Fixed Assets, beside Land, Buildings, Leasehold Improvements, Plant & Equipment, Vehicles & Transport Equipment, Other Fixed Assets and Construction in Progress. Take the class at the amount the balance sheet carries it: net of accumulated depreciation and impairment, as an Ind AS balance sheet prints property, plant and equipment; at cost only where the face itself prints the class at cost with the accumulated depreciation as a separate deduction row, which is then 'Accum Deprec & Impairment(-)'. Not this line: office equipment and computers ('Plant & Equipment'); leasehold improvements ('Leasehold Improvements'). Schedule III prints 'Property, Plant and Equipment' as one row: that row is 'Plant & Equipment' as printed and is not split into classes from the reconciliation of its carrying amount by class, so this line then has no row of its own. Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list.

items.label: Vehicles & Transport Equipment
items.definition: Motor vehicles and other transport equipment the entity holds for its own use — vehicles, vessels, aircraft, containers — as a class of fixed assets printed in a row of its own among the non-current assets of the balance sheet ('Vehicles', 'Motor vehicles', 'Vessels', 'Aircraft'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Gross Fixed Assets, beside Land, Buildings, Leasehold Improvements, Plant & Equipment, Furniture & Fixtures, Other Fixed Assets and Construction in Progress. Take the class at the amount the balance sheet carries it: net of accumulated depreciation and impairment, as an Ind AS balance sheet prints property, plant and equipment; at cost only where the face itself prints the class at cost with the accumulated depreciation as a separate deduction row, which is then 'Accum Deprec & Impairment(-)'. Not this line: vehicles held under leases and carried as right-of-use assets ('Land use rights', where this template places the 'Right-of-use assets' row); vessels or aircraft under construction ('Construction in Progress'). Schedule III prints 'Property, Plant and Equipment' as one row: that row is 'Plant & Equipment' as printed and is not split into classes from the reconciliation of its carrying amount by class, so this line then has no row of its own. Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list.

items.label: Other Fixed Assets
items.definition: Tangible fixed assets other than the named classes, where the balance sheet prints them as rows of their own among the non-current assets: bearer plants, 'Biological assets other than bearer plants', assets held under finance leases printed under that name, and other tangible assets printed apart from property, plant and equipment. Where the balance sheet prints more than one of these rows, cite each; the line is their total. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Gross Fixed Assets, beside Land, Buildings, Leasehold Improvements, Plant & Equipment, Furniture & Fixtures, Vehicles & Transport Equipment and Construction in Progress. Take the class at the amount the balance sheet carries it: net of accumulated depreciation and impairment, as an Ind AS balance sheet prints property, plant and equipment; at cost only where the face itself prints the class at cost with the accumulated depreciation as a separate deduction row, which is then 'Accum Deprec & Impairment(-)'. Not this line: the single Schedule III row 'Property, Plant and Equipment' ('Plant & Equipment'); the Schedule III row 'Right-of-use assets', which this template places on 'Land use rights'; 'Capital work-in-progress' ('Construction in Progress'); 'Investment Property' ('Investment Property(Net)'); intangible assets and 'Intangible assets under development' ('Other Intangible Assets'). An asset class inside the property, plant and equipment row is not split out of it. Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list.

items.label: Construction in Progress
items.definition: Fixed assets still being built or installed and not yet ready for use, as the balance sheet prints them among the non-current assets: the Schedule III row 'Capital work-in-progress' as printed ('Capital work in progress', 'Construction in progress'), including the machinery under installation and project materials its breakdown lists. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Gross Fixed Assets, beside Land, Buildings, Leasehold Improvements, Plant & Equipment, Furniture & Fixtures, Vehicles & Transport Equipment and Other Fixed Assets. It is a printed row; read it as it stands. Not this line: 'Intangible assets under development' ('Other Intangible Assets'); investment property under construction ('Investment Property(Net)'); capital advances paid to suppliers of fixed assets, which Schedule III prints within other non-current assets ('Other Non-Current Assets'); contract assets and work in progress for customers, which are not the entity's own fixed assets; a real estate developer's projects under construction for sale, which are inventory ('WIP'). Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list.

items.label: Gross Fixed Assets
items.definition: The subtotal the filing PRINTS as 'Gross Fixed Assets', reported in the non-current assets section of the balance sheet. It is the sum of Land, Buildings, Leasehold Improvements, Plant & Equipment, Furniture & Fixtures, Vehicles & Transport Equipment, Other Fixed Assets and Construction in Progress. Read the printed subtotal. Do not compute it here and do not replace it with a figure added up from those components: the arithmetic is declared in this template's rollup, and a subtotal the filing states itself is the more authoritative number. Where the filing prints no subtotal on this line, answer with an empty sources list and leave it to the rollup.

items.label: Accum Deprec & Impairment(-)
items.definition: The accumulated depreciation and accumulated impairment losses on the fixed assets this template counts in Gross Fixed Assets, where the balance sheet itself prints them as a deduction row beneath fixed assets carried at cost ('Less: accumulated depreciation', 'Accumulated depreciation and impairment'). Net Fixed Assets is Gross Fixed Assets plus this line, so the template carries it as a negative figure, a deduction. An Ind AS balance sheet prints property, plant and equipment net, and the fixed asset lines then already carry net amounts: answer with an empty sources list, and do not take the accumulated depreciation from the reconciliation of the carrying amount, which would deduct it a second time. Not this line: accumulated amortisation of intangible assets ('Accum Intgbl Assets Amort(-)') or of goodwill ('Accum Goodwill Amortized(-)'); the depreciation charge for the year ('Depreciation and amortisation expense'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Net Fixed Assets.

items.label: Net Fixed Assets
items.definition: Calculate Net Fixed Assets as Gross Fixed Assets plus the reported Accum Deprec & Impairment(-), which is stored as a negative contra-asset and therefore equals gross fixed assets minus depreciation and impairment.

items.label: Goodwill
items.definition: Goodwill arising on business combinations, as the balance sheet prints it among the non-current assets ('Goodwill', 'Goodwill on consolidation'), carried net of accumulated impairment as printed. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Net Intangibles, beside Land use rights, Concessions, Licenses & Trdmrks, Patents, Start-Up Capitalized Expenses, R&D Capitalized Expenses and Other Intangible Assets. It is a printed row; read it as it stands. Not this line: goodwill included in the carrying amount of an investment in an associate or joint venture ('Investments in Associates', 'Invest in JVs & Partnerships'); other intangible assets ('Other Intangible Assets'); capital reserve arising on a bargain purchase, which is equity. Accumulated amortisation of goodwill printed as its own deduction row is 'Accum Goodwill Amortized(-)'. Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list.

items.label: Accum Goodwill Amortized(-)
items.definition: Accumulated amortisation (and accumulated impairment) of goodwill, where the balance sheet prints goodwill at cost with this amount as a separate deduction row beneath it. Ind AS does not amortise goodwill and an Ind AS balance sheet prints goodwill net, so this line is almost always empty. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Net Intangibles, and it is carried as a negative figure, a deduction from Goodwill. Where the balance sheet prints goodwill net, answer with an empty sources list and do not take an accumulated impairment figure from the breakdown of the goodwill row. Not this line: accumulated amortisation of other intangible assets ('Accum Intgbl Assets Amort(-)'), accumulated depreciation of fixed assets ('Accum Deprec & Impairment(-)'), or the impairment charge for the year.

items.label: Land use rights
items.definition: The right to use land for a fixed term, and — in this template — the Ind AS 116 row 'Right-of-use assets' as the balance sheet prints it among the non-current assets ('Right-of-use assets', 'Right of use assets', 'Land use rights'): leasehold land, buildings, plant and vehicles the entity uses under leases, carried at cost less accumulated depreciation. Read the printed row as it stands and do not split it into its classes of leased asset. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Net Intangibles, beside Goodwill, Concessions, Licenses & Trdmrks, Patents, Start-Up Capitalized Expenses, R&D Capitalized Expenses and Other Intangible Assets. Not this line: freehold land ('Land'); land and buildings the entity owns ('Buildings'); leasehold improvements made to leased premises ('Leasehold Improvements'); the lease liabilities that go with these assets ('Lease liabilities(LTP)', 'Lease liabilities(CP)'); land held as investment property ('Investment Property(Net)'). Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list.

items.label: Concessions, Licenses & Trdmrks
items.definition: Service concession rights, licences, franchises, permits, brands and trademarks carried as intangible assets, where the balance sheet prints them as a row of their own among the non-current assets ('Concession rights', 'Licences', 'Brands and trademarks', 'Franchise rights'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Net Intangibles, beside Goodwill, Land use rights, Patents, Start-Up Capitalized Expenses, R&D Capitalized Expenses and Other Intangible Assets. Schedule III prints 'Other Intangible assets' as one row (with 'Goodwill' and 'Intangible assets under development' beside it): that row is 'Other Intangible Assets' as printed and is not split into its kinds from its breakdown. Not this line: patents and technical know-how ('Patents'); computer software and other intangible assets ('Other Intangible Assets'); right-of-use assets ('Land use rights'); goodwill ('Goodwill'). Where the amount is only part of a larger row the balance sheet prints, it has no row of its own: answer with an empty sources list and do not split it out of that row.

items.label: Patents
items.definition: Patents and technical know-how carried as intangible assets, where the balance sheet prints them as a row of their own among the non-current assets ('Patents', 'Technical know-how'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Net Intangibles, beside Goodwill, Land use rights, Concessions, Licenses & Trdmrks, Start-Up Capitalized Expenses, R&D Capitalized Expenses and Other Intangible Assets. Schedule III prints 'Other Intangible assets' as one row (with 'Goodwill' and 'Intangible assets under development' beside it): that row is 'Other Intangible Assets' as printed and is not split into its kinds from its breakdown. Where the amount is only part of a larger row the balance sheet prints, it has no row of its own: answer with an empty sources list and do not split it out of that row.

items.label: Start-Up Capitalized Expenses
items.definition: Pre-operative and start-up costs that the entity has capitalised and carries as an asset, where the balance sheet prints them as a row of their own among the non-current assets ('Start-up costs', 'Preliminary expenses', 'Pre-operative expenses'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Net Intangibles, beside Goodwill, Land use rights, Concessions, Licenses & Trdmrks, Patents, R&D Capitalized Expenses and Other Intangible Assets. items.label: R&D Capitalized Expenses
items.definition: Development expenditure the entity has capitalised as an asset, where the balance sheet prints it as a row of its own among the non-current assets ('Development costs', 'Deferred development costs', 'Product development'). Where the amount is only part of a larger row the balance sheet prints, it has no row of its own: answer with an empty sources list and do not split it out of that row.

items.label: Other Intangible Assets
items.definition: Intangible assets other than goodwill, as the balance sheet prints them among the non-current assets: the Schedule III row 'Other Intangible assets' as printed (with the software, licences, brands and other rights it contains), and the row 'Intangible assets under development' printed beside it. Where both rows are printed, cite each; the line is their total. Read each row as it stands and do not split its kinds out of it. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Net Intangibles, beside Goodwill, Land use rights, Concessions, Licenses & Trdmrks, Patents, Start-Up Capitalized Expenses and R&D Capitalized Expenses. Not this line: goodwill ('Goodwill'); the Schedule III row 'Right-of-use assets' ('Land use rights'); 'Capital work-in-progress' on tangible assets ('Construction in Progress'); capital advances ('Other Non-Current Assets'). items.label: Investment Property(Net)
items.definition: Land and buildings held to earn rentals or for capital appreciation rather than for own use or sale, as the balance sheet prints them among the non-current assets: the Schedule III row 'Investment Property' ('Investment properties'), carried at cost less accumulated depreciation as Ind AS requires, and investment property under construction where printed with it. It is a printed row; read it as it stands. Not this line: owner-occupied property ('Buildings', 'Plant & Equipment'); land and buildings held for development and sale, which are inventory; right-of-use assets ('Land use rights'); investment property classified as held for sale ('Assets Related to Disc Ops'). It is a printed row; read it as it stands. Not this line: loans to and amounts due from subsidiaries ('Due from subsidiaries'); investments in associates and joint ventures ('Investments in Associates', 'Invest in JVs & Partnerships'); other equity and debt investments held as financial assets ('Secur & Other Fincl Assets(LTP)'). Where one 'Investments' row carries subsidiaries together with other investments, it is not split here. A consolidated balance sheet prints no such row: answer with an empty sources list. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Non-Current Assets.

items.label: Due from Related Parties(LTP)
items.definition: Amounts receivable from related parties — fellow subsidiaries, holding companies, shareholders, directors, associates, joint ventures and other related parties — INCLUDING trade receivables from them, NET of any loss allowance. EXCLUDES ENTRUSTED LOANS, amounts payable to related parties, transaction amounts for the year, guarantees, and the. Report the largest of three readings of the one balance: the related-party rows of the balance sheet, the related-party rows inside the receivable notes, and the related-party note's receivables net of their allowance.

cascade.note: MAX_VALID(Find 1, Find 2, Find 3) — the spec's own selection rule, now expressible. The three Finds are three readings of ONE quantity and the fullest disclosure wins, which is why this is a maximum and not a sum: summing them would count the same related-party receivable up to three times. Every term is `any_of`, so a filing that discloses only one of the three still answers with that one, and a filing that discloses none leaves the line empty rather than publishing zero (spec 3.6). `outranks_printed` because no balance sheet prints this quantity: it is related-party amounts extracted from within four receivable captions, net of entrusted loans, and a caption binding this line found something else. This replaces six first-available rungs whose own note recorded that they could not express the rule.

items.label: Secur & Other Fincl Assets(LTP)
items.definition: Securities and other financial assets held as NON-CURRENT assets — the same classes of investment as the current portion (fair value through profit or loss or other comprehensive income, equity and debt securities, bonds, funds, wealth management products) but not expected to be realised within one year, including the non-current portion of a holding a note splits between current and non-current. Excludes derivatives, other receivables, and investments in related parties, associates and joint ventures. The non-current securities and other financial assets (Find 1 LTP) less the Level 3 amount the current line could not absorb.

cascade.note: Find 1 LTP less the current line's overshoot. Find 1 LTP is the eight non-current parts, each already the sum of a note's NON-CURRENT line items with derivatives, other receivables and associate/JV/related-party investments left out — so there is no Find 2 and no split row to take afterwards. Each part is `any_of`, so a filing printing only some of these notes sums the ones it prints. The overshoot (`sub__fa_cp_intermediate_residual`, Find 3 − Find 1 of the current line) is the Level 3 amount the current line could not absorb, and is `required`: without an overshoot this rung does not resolve and LTP_P2 answers. Passed over below zero.
Find 1 LTP with no carry-forward: the current line did not overshoot, or deducting the overshoot went below zero. Passed over below zero — a negative carrying amount is not a figure a filing asserts.

FALLBACK TO THE FACE, for a filing whose notes give none of Find 1 LTP: the printed non-current FVTPL / FVTOCI / other non-current financial assets / debt investments row through its face part. LAST, so it never displaces a note reading.

items.label: Other Non-Current Assets

Where the balance sheet prints more than one such row, cite each; the line is their total. It is the residual line of the section: where a part with a line of its own is inside a row you cite, the template's rollup takes it out — do not deduct it yourself. Not this line: the total of non-current assets ('Total Non-Current Assets') or total assets; any row printed among current assets, liabilities or equity; a row that has its own line here, such as non-current 'Investments' and 'Other financial assets' ('Secur & Other Fincl Assets(LTP)'), non-current 'Loans' ('Other Receivables(LTP)'), 'Deferred tax assets (net)' ('Deferred Tax Assets'), investments in joint ventures ('Invest in JVs & Partnerships') or in subsidiaries ('Investment in Subsidiaries'). Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Non-Current Assets.

It is a printed row; read it as it stands. Do not gross it up from the breakdown of deferred tax before offset. Not this line: the deferred tax charge or credit for the year in profit or loss; advance income tax net of provisions ('Income tax assets (net)', 'Current Tax Assets (Net)'); deferred tax liabilities ('Deferred Tax Liability'). Read the printed row. It is the sum of Net Fixed Assets, Net Intangibles, Investment Property(Net), Investment in Subsidiaries, Investments in Associates, Invest in JVs & Partnerships, Due from directors, Due from subsidiaries and and 7 more. Read the printed subtotal. Do not compute it here and do not replace it with a figure added up from those components: the arithmetic is declared in this template's rollup, and a subtotal the filing states itself is the more authoritative number. items.label: Raw materials

It is a part of Inventories. Schedule III prints 'Inventories' as one row on the face and gives raw materials, work-in-progress, finished goods, stock-in-trade, stores and spares and goods in transit in its breakdown: that face row is 'Inventories', and this line has no figure of its own unless the face itself prints the class as a row; do not split the total yourself. items.label: WIP
items.definition: Inventory in the course of production — 'Work-in-progress', 'Work in progress', semi-finished goods — and, for a real estate developer, projects under development held for sale in the ordinary course of business ('Construction work-in-progress' of projects for sale, 'Properties under development'), printed as a row in the current assets section. It is a part of Inventories. Schedule III prints 'Inventories' as one row on the face and gives raw materials, work-in-progress, finished goods, stock-in-trade, stores and spares and goods in transit in its breakdown: that face row is 'Inventories', and this line has no figure of its own unless the face itself prints the class as a row; do not split the total yourself. Its peers are 'Raw materials' and 'Finished goods'. Not this line: 'Capital work-in-progress' on the entity's own fixed assets ('Construction in Progress'); investment property under construction ('Investment Property(Net)'); contract assets and unbilled revenue on construction contracts ('Other Current Assets').

items.label: Finished goods
items.definition: Inventory ready for sale — finished goods, 'Stock-in-trade' (goods bought for resale), goods in transit and, for a real estate developer, completed units held for sale — printed as a row in the current assets section ('Finished goods', 'Stock-in-trade', 'Traded goods'). It is a part of Inventories. Schedule III prints 'Inventories' as one row on the face and gives raw materials, work-in-progress, finished goods, stock-in-trade, stores and spares and goods in transit in its breakdown: that face row is 'Inventories', and this line has no figure of its own unless the face itself prints the class as a row; do not split the total yourself. Its peers are 'Raw materials' and 'WIP'. Not this line: investment property ('Investment Property(Net)'); assets classified as held for sale under Ind AS 105 ('Assets Related to Disc Ops'), even where the caption says 'held for sale'.

Read the printed subtotal. Do not compute it here and do not replace it with a figure added up from those components: the arithmetic is declared in this template's rollup, and a subtotal the filing states itself is the more authoritative number. items.label: Short Term Securities
items.definition: Marketable securities held as a current asset, where the balance sheet prints them in a row captioned as short-term securities or short-term investments ('Short-term investments', 'Marketable securities') apart from the Schedule III current financial asset 'Investments'. Read the printed row. The Schedule III current 'Investments' row — mutual fund units, bonds, debentures and other investments at fair value through profit or loss or at amortised cost — is 'Secur & Other Fincl Assets(CP)', not this line. Not this line: derivative assets; deposits with banks ('Pledged Deposits', 'Cash Equivalents'); current 'Loans' and 'Other financial assets' ('Other Receivables(CP)'). Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Current Assets.

items.label: Secur & Other Fincl Assets(CP)
items.definition: Securities and other financial assets held as CURRENT assets — financial assets at fair value through profit or loss and through other comprehensive income, listed and unlisted equity and debt securities, corporate and government bonds, investment and money market funds, wealth management products, structured deposits and certificates of deposit, expected to be realised within one year. Excludes derivative assets, other receivables, and cash and cash equivalents. The current securities and other financial assets (Find 1) less the Level 3 fair-value total (Find 3), floored at zero.

cascade.note: Find 1 − Find 3. Find 1 is the six current parts, each already the sum of a note's CURRENT line items with derivatives and other receivables left out — so there is no Find 2 and no non-current deduction to take afterwards. Each part is `any_of`, so a filing printing only some of these notes sums the ones it prints. Find 3 (Level 3) is an `adjustment`, so a filing with no fair value hierarchy table subtracts nothing. PASSED OVER WHEN IT COMPUTES BELOW ZERO, and the next rung then publishes zero.

Zero WHEN FIND 1 − FIND 3 WENT BELOW ZERO, and only then. `sub__fa_cp_intermediate_residual` resolves only in that case (it is Find 3 − Find 1, passed over when negative), so min(0, residual) is 0 exactly where the rule says "treat Find 1 as Find 3 and make this field zero"; the overshoot itself is carried to Securities (LTP). AHEAD OF THE FACE, so an overshoot publishes zero rather than falling through to the printed row.

FALLBACK TO THE FACE, for a filing whose notes give none of Find 1: the printed current trading / FVTPL row through its face part. `derived` keys are unmatchable by caption, so without this part the printed row reached no column and the residual sweep filed it on the section's catch-all. LAST, so it never displaces a note reading, and after CP_ZERO, so a Level 3 overshoot publishes zero rather than the face.

items.label: Current Tax Receivables
items.definition: Income tax the entity has paid in advance or is owed by the tax authorities, net of the provision for tax, and expects to recover within one year: the Schedule III row 'Current Tax Assets (Net)' printed in the current assets section ('Current tax assets (net)', 'Income tax assets (net)', 'Advance income tax (net of provisions)'). Read the printed row. Not this line: a non-current tax asset printed among the non-current assets ('Income tax assets (net)' or 'Non-current tax assets (net)' under that heading), which is 'Other Non-Current Assets' as printed; deferred tax assets ('Deferred Tax Assets'); balances with government authorities for GST and other indirect taxes inside 'Other current assets' ('Other Current Assets'); a row captioned only as prepaid tax ('Prepayments(CP)'); current tax liabilities ('Current Tax Payable'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Current Assets.

items.label: Prepayments(CP)
items.definition: Amounts paid in advance for goods, services and assets not yet received, held as a current asset, where the balance sheet prints them as a row of their own: 'Prepayments', 'Prepaid expenses', 'Advances to suppliers', 'Advance to vendors', purchase and trade deposits paid, and a row captioned as prepaid tax. Read the printed row. On an Ind AS balance sheet these advances usually sit inside the Schedule III row 'Other current assets', which is 'Other Current Assets' as printed: this line then has no row of its own, and the advances are not split out of that row. items.definition: A non-current loan from a controlling or other shareholder, as the balance sheet prints it under non-current liabilities.

items.label: Loan from the holding company, on the face of the balance sheet
items.definition: A non-current loan from the parent or ultimate holding company, as the balance sheet prints it under non-current liabilities. Excludes loans from third parties.

items.label: Lease liabilities(LTP)
items.definition: The NON-CURRENT portion of lease liabilities recognised under Ind AS 116 — the present value of the lease payments due after more than one year — as the balance sheet prints it among the non-current financial liabilities: the Schedule III row 'Lease liabilities' under non-current liabilities. It is a printed row; read it as it stands. Not this line: 'Lease liabilities' under current liabilities ('Lease liabilities(CP)'); finance lease obligations printed under that older name ('Finance Leases(LTP)'); right-of-use assets ('Land use rights'). Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Non-Current Liabilities.

items.label: Other Non-Current Liabilities
items.definition: The non-current liabilities the balance sheet prints that have no more specific line in this template, as printed: the Schedule III row 'Other non-current liabilities' (deferred government grants, advances and income received in advance and the like where the face combines them, cited as printed and not split into its breakdown), the non-current 'Other financial liabilities' row (security deposits received, retention money, payables for capital goods), and other rows of the non-current liabilities section that no other line names. Where the balance sheet prints more than one such row, cite each; the line is their total. It is the residual line of the section: where a part with a line of its own is inside a row you cite, the template's rollup takes it out — do not deduct it yourself. Not this line: the total of non-current liabilities or total liabilities; a row that has its own line here, such as 'Borrowings' ('LTD Bank'), 'Lease liabilities' ('Lease liabilities(LTP)'), non-current 'Trade payables' ('Trade Payables(LTP)'), 'Provisions' ('Other Provisions(LTP)'), 'Deferred tax liabilities (net)' ('Deferred Tax Liability') or non-current 'Contract liabilities' ('Customer Advances(LTP)'). Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Non-Current Liabilities.

items.label: Customer Advances(LTP)
items.definition: Amounts received from customers in advance for goods or services the entity will deliver after more than one year, printed as a row of their own among the non-current liabilities: non-current 'Contract liabilities', 'Advances from customers', 'Income received in advance'. The part due within one year is a current-liabilities line, not this one. Where such advances sit inside 'Other non-current liabilities', that row is 'Other Non-Current Liabilities' as printed and they are not split out. Not this line: deferred government grants ('Deferred Income(LTP)'); security deposits received from customers, dealers or tenants, which are financial liabilities ('Other Non-Current Liabilities'). Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Non-Current Liabilities.

items.label: Deferred Income(LTP)
items.definition: Deferred income classified as non-current — mainly government grants to be released to profit or loss over the lives of the related assets — where the balance sheet prints it as a row of its own among the non-current liabilities ('Deferred government grants', 'Deferred income', 'Deferred revenue'). Where the grants sit inside 'Other non-current liabilities', that row is 'Other Non-Current Liabilities' as printed and they are not split out. Not this line: deferred income under current liabilities ('Deferred Income(CP)'); contract liabilities and customer advances ('Customer Advances(LTP)'); deferred tax liabilities ('Deferred Tax Liability'). Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Non-Current Liabilities.

items.label: Trade Payables(LTP)
items.definition: Trade payables (amounts owed to suppliers for goods and services) due after more than one year, where the balance sheet prints them as a row of their own among the non-current financial liabilities ('Trade payables' under non-current liabilities, with its split between micro and small enterprises and other creditors where printed). Not this line: trade payables under current liabilities ('Trade Payables(CP)'); retention money and payables for capital goods within non-current 'Other financial liabilities' ('Other Non-Current Liabilities'). Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Non-Current Liabilities.

items.label: Retirement Benefits(LTP)
items.definition: Post-employment and other long-term employee benefit obligations due after more than one year — gratuity, compensated absences, pension and post-retirement medical obligations — where the balance sheet prints them as a row of their own among the non-current liabilities ('Employee benefit obligations', 'Provision for employee benefits', 'Provision for gratuity'). Schedule III usually prints them inside the non-current 'Provisions' row: that row is 'Other Provisions(LTP)' as printed, and the employee benefits are not split out of it to this line. Not this line: salaries and wages payable and other current employee dues; a defined benefit surplus recognised as an asset; the current obligation ('Retirement Benefits(CP)'). Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Non-Current Liabilities.

items.label: Deferred Tax Liability
items.definition: Deferred tax liabilities recognised for taxable temporary differences, as the balance sheet prints them among the non-current liabilities ('Deferred tax liabilities (net)', 'Deferred tax liabilities'), after any offset against deferred tax assets that the balance sheet itself makes. It is a printed row; read it as it stands. Do not gross it up from the breakdown of deferred tax before offset. Not this line: the deferred tax charge for the year in profit or loss; 'Current Tax Liabilities (Net)' ('Current Tax Payable'); deferred tax assets ('Deferred Tax Assets'); deferred government grants ('Deferred Income(LTP)'). Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Non-Current Liabilities.

items.label: Other Provisions(LTP)
items.definition: Provisions classified as non-current: the Schedule III non-current row 'Provisions' as printed ('Long-term provisions'), with whatever its breakdown lists — employee benefits, decommissioning and site restoration, warranties, litigation and the like — read as one row and not split; and other non-current provision rows the face prints on their own. Where the balance sheet prints more than one such row, cite each; the line is their total. Not this line: employee benefit obligations printed as a row of their own ('Retirement Benefits(LTP)'); provisions under current liabilities ('Other Provisions(CP)'); impairment allowances against assets; deferred tax liabilities ('Deferred Tax Liability'). Where the balance sheet prints no such row, answer with an empty sources list. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Non-Current Liabilities.

items.label: Total Non-Current Liabilities
items.definition: The subtotal the filing PRINTS as 'Total Non-Current Liabilities', reported in the non-current liabilities section of the balance sheet. It is the sum of LTD Bank, LTD Other, LTD Convertible, Finance Leases(LTP), Due to Related Parties(LTP), Lease liabilities(LTP), Other Non-Current Liabilities, Customer Advances(LTP) and and 5 more. Read the printed subtotal. Do not compute it here and do not replace it with a figure added up from those components: the arithmetic is declared in this template's rollup, and a subtotal the filing states itself is the more authoritative number. Where the filing prints no subtotal on this line, answer with an empty sources list and leave it to the rollup.

items.label: CPLTD Bank
items.definition: The current maturities of long-term borrowings — the part of term loans and other long-term debt that falls due within one year — where the balance sheet prints it as a row of its own in the current liabilities section ('Current maturities of long-term borrowings', 'Current maturities of long-term debt'). Where the filing prints that portion in several rows, this line is their total, and where a row you cite takes in debt this template carries on lines of its own, its rollup takes that debt out: do not deduct it yourself. Schedule III includes the current maturities within the current 'Borrowings' row, and that row is 'ST Bank Loans Payable' as printed: where the current maturities are only part of it, this line has no row of its own; do not split them out of it. Not this line: the current 'Borrowings' row ('ST Bank Loans Payable'); current 'Lease liabilities' ('Lease liabilities(CP)'); interest accrued on borrowings ('Interest Payable', or 'Other Current Liabilities' where it sits inside 'Other financial liabilities'). The part due after one year is 'LTD Bank'. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Current Liabilities.

items.label: CPLTD Other
items.definition: The current maturities of long-term debt other than bank loans — debentures, bonds and notes, and loans from financial institutions and other lenders falling due within one year — where the balance sheet prints them as a row of their own in the current liabilities section ('Current maturities of debentures', 'Current maturities of non-convertible debentures'). Where the face prints the same instrument under both current and non-current liabilities, this line is the current row; the non-current row is 'LTD Other'. Where the current maturities are only part of the Schedule III current 'Borrowings' row, that row is 'ST Bank Loans Payable' as printed and they are not split out to this line. Not this line: current maturities of bank term loans ('CPLTD Bank'); short-term loans ('ST Bank Loans Payable', 'ST Other Loans Payable'); current 'Lease liabilities' ('Lease liabilities(CP)'). It is one of the debt lines this template's rollup takes out of CPLTD Bank and adds into Total Current Liabilities.

items.label: ST Bank Loans Payable
items.definition: Short-term borrowings repayable within one year, reported among the current financial liabilities of the balance sheet: the Schedule III current row 'Borrowings' as printed ('Short-term borrowings', 'Working capital loans from banks'), whatever its breakdown lists — loans repayable on demand, cash credit and overdrafts, working capital demand loans, packing credit, commercial paper and the current maturities of long-term borrowings, secured and unsecured together. Read the printed row and do not split it into its breakdown. Not this line: current maturities of long-term debt printed as a row of their own ('CPLTD Bank', 'CPLTD Other'); short-term loans from lenders other than banks printed as a row of their own ('ST Other Loans Payable'); current 'Lease liabilities' ('Lease liabilities(CP)'); trade payables including acceptances ('Trade Payables(CP)'); the non-current 'Borrowings' row ('LTD Bank'). It is one of the debt lines this template's rollup takes out of CPLTD Bank and adds into Total Current Liabilities.

items.label: ST Other Loans Payable
items.definition: Short-term loans from lenders other than banks — commercial paper, inter-corporate deposits, loans from financial institutions, other parties and government — repayable within one year, where the balance sheet prints them as a row of their own in the current liabilities section ('Commercial paper', 'Inter-corporate deposits', 'Short-term loans from others'). Where they are only part of the Schedule III current 'Borrowings' row, that row is 'ST Bank Loans Payable' as printed and this line has no row of its own; do not split them out of it. Not this line: bank loans ('ST Bank Loans Payable', 'CPLTD Bank'); current maturities of debentures and bonds ('CPLTD Other'); amounts due to related parties ('Due to Related Parties(CP)'). It is one of the debt lines this template's rollup takes out of CPLTD Bank and adds into Total Current Liabilities.

items.label: Finance Leases(CP)

items.label: Due to Related Parties(CP)
items.definition: Current amounts the company owes to related parties other than for goods and services bought — to the holding company, fellow subsidiaries, associates, joint ventures and other related companies — such as non-trade payables, advances, current accounts, and interest and dividends payable to them. The figure comes first from the related party disclosure of outstanding balances, its amounts payable under a 'Due to related parties' or similar heading; where that disclosure gives none, it is the current-liabilities row the balance sheet prints as 'Due to related parties' or 'Amounts due to related parties'. items.label: Other Current Liabilities

items.label: Deferred Income(CP)
items.definition: Income received or receivable that will be recognised in profit or loss within the next year, held as a current liability, where the balance sheet prints it as a row of its own: the current part of government grants not yet recognised ('Deferred government grants') and other deferred income or deferred revenue ('Deferred income', 'Deferred revenue'). Read the printed row. Where it sits inside 'Other current liabilities', that row is 'Other Current Liabilities' as printed and it is not split out. items.label: Current Tax Payable
items.definition: Income tax the company owes on its profits, net of advance tax paid, and expects to settle within one year: the Schedule III row 'Current Tax Liabilities (Net)' printed in the current liabilities section ('Current tax liabilities (net)', 'Income tax liabilities (net)', 'Income tax payable'). Read the printed row. A row captioned as a provision for taxation ('Provision for tax', 'Provision for taxation') is 'Tax Provision(CP)'. Not this line: GST, TDS and other statutory dues payable within 'Other current liabilities' ('Other Current Liabilities'); deferred tax liabilities ('Deferred Tax Liability'); 'Current Tax Assets (Net)', which is an asset ('Current Tax Receivables'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Current Liabilities.

items.label: Interest Payable
items.definition: Interest accrued on borrowings, debentures and other interest-bearing liabilities and not yet paid at the balance sheet date, where the balance sheet prints it as a row of its own in the current liabilities section ('Interest accrued', 'Interest accrued but not due on borrowings', 'Interest payable'). Read the printed row. Schedule III places interest accrued within the current 'Other financial liabilities', which is 'Other Current Liabilities' as printed: where it is only part of that row, this line has no row of its own; do not split it out. Not this line: dividends payable ('Dividends Payable'); interest expense for the year ('Interest Expense(-)'); the borrowings themselves. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Current Liabilities.

items.label: Dividends Payable
items.definition: Dividends the company has declared to its shareholders that remain unpaid at the balance sheet date, and unclaimed dividends, where the balance sheet prints them as a row of their own in the current liabilities section ('Dividend payable', 'Unpaid dividends', 'Unclaimed dividends'). Read the printed row. Schedule III places unpaid dividends within the current 'Other financial liabilities', which is 'Other Current Liabilities' as printed: where they are only part of that row, this line has no row of its own; do not split them out. Not this line: a dividend proposed after the year end and not yet approved, which is not a liability ('Proposed Cash Dividends'); dividends paid or declared during the year; interest payable ('Interest Payable'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Current Liabilities.

items.label: Trade payables- related parties
items.definition: Trade payables owed to related parties — the holding company, fellow subsidiaries, associates, joint ventures and other related companies — for goods and services bought, held as a current liability, where the balance sheet prints them as a row of their own ('Trade payables- related parties', 'Trade payables to related parties'). Read the printed row. Where they are only part of the Schedule III 'Trade payables' rows, those rows are 'Trade Payables(CP)' as printed and the related-party part is not split out. Not this line: non-trade amounts due to related parties ('Due to Related Parties(CP)'); borrowings from related parties; trade payables to third parties ('Trade Payables(CP)'); amounts receivable from related parties. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Current Liabilities.

items.label: Trade and other payables(CP)
items.definition: Current payables that the balance sheet prints in ONE row together with trade payables: 'Trade and other payables', 'Creditors and other payables', 'Trade payables and other financial liabilities'. Schedule III presents trade payables as rows of their own, so on an Ind AS balance sheet this row is uncommon. Read the printed row. Where trade payables are printed in rows of their own, those rows are 'Trade Payables(CP)', and related-party trade payables printed apart are 'Trade payables- related parties'. Not this line: the Schedule III 'Trade payables' rows alone ('Trade Payables(CP)'); current 'Other financial liabilities' and 'Other current liabilities' printed on their own ('Other Current Liabilities'); contract liabilities and advances from customers ('Customer Advances(CP)'); amounts due to related parties printed on their own ('Due to Related Parties(CP)'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Current Liabilities.

items.label: Trade Payables(CP)
items.definition: Amounts owed to suppliers for goods and services bought in the ordinary course of business, held as a current liability: the Schedule III current financial liability 'Trade payables' ('Trade Payables', 'Creditors', 'Sundry creditors', acceptances where the face includes them). Not this line: a row combining trade payables with other payables ('Trade and other payables(CP)'); trade payables to related parties printed apart ('Trade payables- related parties'); payables for capital goods and employee dues within 'Other financial liabilities' ('Other Current Liabilities'); contract liabilities and advances from customers ('Customer Advances(CP)'); the non-current balance ('Trade Payables(LTP)'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Total Current Liabilities.

Not this line: dividends recognised in the year ('Cash Div Common Shares(-)'); a dividend declared and unpaid at the year end ('Dividends Payable'); the dividend per share.

items.label: Cash Div Common Shares(-)
items.definition: Dividends to equity shareholders charged to retained earnings in the year: final and interim dividends declared and recognised, and special dividends — rows such as 'Final dividend', 'Interim dividend', 'Dividends paid', 'Dividend on equity shares', with the dividend distribution tax on them where the filing prints it beside them. It is a movement of the year in retained earnings, read from the retained earnings column of the statement of changes in equity. Read the printed row; it reduces retained earnings. Not this line: the cash paid for dividends ('Dividends Paid(Fin)'); a final dividend proposed after the year end and not recognised in it ('Proposed Cash Dividends'); dividends on preference shares ('Cash Div Pref Shares(-)'); bonus shares ('Stock Dividends(NC)(-)'); dividends paid by subsidiaries to non-controlling shareholders. It is one of the movements this template's rollup takes out of Other Adj to Retained Profits.

items.label: Stock Dividends(NC)(-)
items.definition: Capitalisation of retained earnings into share capital: bonus shares issued out of retained earnings ('Issue of bonus shares', 'Bonus issue', 'Capitalised for issue of bonus shares'), and any dividend settled in shares rather than cash, as the retained earnings column prints it. It is a movement of the year in retained earnings, read from the retained earnings column of the statement of changes in equity. Read the printed row; it reduces retained earnings. Not this line: bonus shares issued out of securities premium or general reserve, which do not move retained earnings; cash dividends ('Cash Div Common Shares(-)'); shares issued for cash or on the exercise of options; transfers to reserves ('Transfer to Reserves(-)'). It is one of the movements this template's rollup takes out of Other Adj to Retained Profits.

It is a movement of the year in retained earnings, read from the retained earnings column of the statement of changes in equity. Read the printed row: a transfer to reserves reduces retained earnings and a transfer from reserves adds to them. Not this line: dividends; bonus shares ('Stock Dividends(NC)(-)'); the reserve balances themselves ('Capital & Restricted Reserves'); remeasurements of defined benefit plans transferred to retained earnings ('Other Adj to Retained Profits'). items.label: Net Profit/(Loss)
items.definition: The profit or loss the indirect-method operating section starts from: the first row of the operating activities section of the cash flow statement, before any adjustment. An Ind AS cash flow statement usually starts from the profit before tax ('Profit before tax', 'Profit before tax from continuing operations', 'Profit/(loss) before tax'); some start from the profit for the year after tax, and either is this line as printed. Where the statement starts from profit before tax for continuing and for discontinued operations in two rows, this line is their total. Take the figure as the statement prints it for the whole group, not the profit attributable to owners of the company. Not this line: the income tax added back below a profit-after-tax starting row ('Income Tax Expense'); 'Operating profit before working capital changes', a subtotal printed further down. It is a printed row; where the section prints no starting profit, answer with an empty sources list. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Cash Flows Oper Activ(Indirect).

items.label: Income Tax Expense
items.definition: The income tax expense added back in the indirect-method operating section, where the reconciliation starts from the profit for the year after tax: a row such as 'Tax expense', 'Income tax expense' or 'Current and deferred tax' printed among the adjustments to that profit. It is the charge the statement of profit and loss recognised, current and deferred together, not the tax paid in cash. Where the reconciliation starts from the profit before tax — usual on an Ind AS statement — there is no tax add-back and this line is empty. Not this line: 'Income taxes paid (net of refunds)' ('Income Taxes Paid(Indirect)'). It is a printed row; where the section prints none, answer with an empty sources list. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Cash Flows Oper Activ(Indirect).

items.label: Depreciation
items.definition: Depreciation added back to profit in the indirect-method operating section: depreciation of property, plant and equipment, of right-of-use assets and of investment property — 'Depreciation', 'Depreciation of property, plant and equipment', 'Depreciation of right-of-use assets'. Where the filing prints depreciation in several rows (by class of asset), this line is their total; where it prints one combined row for depreciation and amortisation, as an Ind AS statement usually does ('Depreciation and amortisation expense', 'Depreciation, amortisation and impairment expense'), that row is this line as printed and is not split. Not this line: amortisation of intangible assets and impairment losses printed on rows of their own ('Amortization & Asset Impairment'); the profit or loss on sale of property, plant and equipment ('Other Non-Cash Adjs(Oper)'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Cash Flows Oper Activ(Indirect).

items.label: Amortization & Asset Impairment

items.label: Interest Inc Received(Oper)
items.definition: Interest received in cash that the cash flow statement prints within its operating activities section, as a financial-services entity classifies it — a row 'Interest received' below 'Cash generated from operations' or within the operating receipts. The 'Interest income' deducted among the adjustments to profit is the reversal of a credit in profit or loss, not cash received, and is not this line (it falls to 'Other Non-Cash Adjs(Oper)'). items.label: Interest Expense
items.definition: The finance costs added back to profit among the adjustments of the indirect-method operating section: 'Finance costs', 'Interest expense', 'Interest expense on lease liabilities'. Where several such rows are printed this line is their total. It is the charge recognised in profit, not cash paid: interest paid in cash is 'Interest Paid(Fin)' when printed in the financing section, as Ind AS statements usually print it, and 'Interest Paid(Oper)' when printed in the operating section. Not this line: 'Interest income' deducted among the adjustments, which falls to 'Other Non-Cash Adjs(Oper)'; unrealised exchange differences printed on a row of their own. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Cash Flows Oper Activ(Indirect).

items.label: Chg in Trade Receivables
items.definition: The (increase)/decrease in trade receivables: a movement in working capital printed in the indirect-method operating section, between the 'Operating profit before working capital changes' and 'Cash generated from operations' — '(Increase)/decrease in trade receivables', 'Decrease in trade receivables'. Where the filing prints one row for trade and other receivables together ('(Increase)/decrease in trade and other receivables'), that row is this line as printed and is not split. Not this line: other financial assets, loans and other assets printed on their own rows ('Chg in Other Current Assets'); the allowance for expected credit loss, which is an adjustment to profit ('Amortization & Asset Impairment'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Cash Flows Oper Activ(Indirect).

items.label: Chg in Inventories

For a real estate developer the projects it builds for sale are its inventories, so a movement in them printed on its own row is this line too; where several such rows are printed this line is their total. Not this line: a write-down of inventories to net realisable value, which is an adjustment to profit ('Amortization & Asset Impairment'); additions to investment property, which are investing cash flows ('Purchase Investment Property'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Cash Flows Oper Activ(Indirect).

items.label: Chg in Other Current Assets
items.definition: The (increase)/decrease in assets other than trade receivables and inventories: a movement in working capital printed in the indirect-method operating section, between the 'Operating profit before working capital changes' and 'Cash generated from operations' — '(Increase)/decrease in other financial assets', '(Increase)/decrease in other assets', '(Increase)/decrease in loans', '(Increase)/decrease in other current assets', and a movement in contract assets. Where such a row takes in non-current balances too, it is this line as printed and is not split. Where several such rows are printed this line is their total. Not this line: trade receivables ('Chg in Trade Receivables'); inventories ('Chg in Inventories'); movements in bank balances other than cash and cash equivalents printed under investing activities ('Other Invest Cash Flows'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Cash Flows Oper Activ(Indirect).

items.label: Chg in Trade Payables
items.definition: The increase/(decrease) in trade payables: a movement in working capital printed in the indirect-method operating section, between the 'Operating profit before working capital changes' and 'Cash generated from operations' — 'Increase/(decrease) in trade payables', including acceptances. Where the filing prints one row for trade and other payables together ('Increase/(decrease) in trade and other payables'), that row is this line as printed and is not split. Not this line: other financial liabilities, other liabilities and contract liabilities printed on their own rows ('Chg in Other Current Liab'); provisions ('Chg in Provisions'). It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Cash Flows Oper Activ(Indirect).

items.label: Chg in Provisions

items.label: Chg in Other Current Liab

Where such a row takes in non-current balances too, it is this line as printed and is not split. Where several such rows are printed this line is their total. Not this line: trade payables, or trade and other payables printed as one row ('Chg in Trade Payables'); provisions ('Chg in Provisions'); borrowings, which are financing cash flows. It is one of the lines this template's rollup adds into Cash Flows Oper Activ(Indirect).

Where the statement prints taxes paid and refunds received in separate rows, this line is their total. It is cash paid, not the charge: the tax expense added back is 'Income Tax Expense'. items.label: Interest Paid(Oper)
items.definition: Interest paid in cash that the cash flow statement prints within its operating activities section, as a financial-services entity classifies it — 'Interest paid', 'Finance costs paid' below 'Cash generated from operations'. items.label: Other Non-Cash Adjs(Oper)
items.definition: The operating section's remainder: every row printed on the face of the indirect-method operating section — an adjustment to profit or a working-capital movement — that no dedicated line of this template claims, such as share-based payment expense, unrealised foreign exchange differences, '(Profit)/loss on sale of property, plant and equipment (net)', net gain on financial assets at fair value through profit or loss, 'Interest income' and 'Dividend income' deducted, the share of profit of associates and joint ventures, liabilities no longer required written back, and exceptional items adjusted. Its figure is the sum of those rows at their printed signs, each kept with its own caption; it is never worked out as the printed subtotal less the lines the template has mapped. This template's rollup adds it into Cash Flows Oper Activ(Indirect). Not this line: any subtotal or total — 'Operating profit before working capital changes', 'Cash generated from operations', the net cash flow from operating activities ('Cash Flows Oper Activ(Indirect)'); a row a dedicated line takes. Where a row fits a dedicated line, it belongs to that line and not here; do not add this line up yourself.

cascade.note: Find 3 − Find 1: the securities expression with every sign inverted. PASSED OVER WHEN NEGATIVE, so it carries a figure only where Find 1 − Find 3 came out at or below zero — the filings where the current line publishes zero — and that figure is the Level 3 amount Find 1 could not absorb. cascade.note: The NON-CURRENT related-party receivable rows the balance sheet prints, added up. Every term is `any_of`, so a filing disclosing one of them resolves the rung and one disclosing none leaves Find 1 empty rather than publishing zero. WHY ONLY THE NON-CURRENT ONES. This Find feeds `bs_nca__due_from_related_parties_ltp`, which the template rolls up into total non-current assets, while every CURRENT related-party receivable column (`bs_ca__due_from_related_parties_cp`, the JV and partnership line, the related-party trade receivable and the trade-and-other aggregate) is a child of total CURRENT assets and publishes in its own right. Adding those here puts one balance in both sections. Measured on China SCE, whose face prints a single "Due from related parties" 4,065,231 under CURRENT ASSETS: with them, the non-current children summed to 52,567,208 against a printed 49,227,234 — an overshoot of 3,339,974; without them the residual is -725,257, which is the ordinary under-extraction. The parent is not a term either — it selects between the three Finds, so naming it here would be a cycle. BOTH MATURITIES IS THE DECLARED INTENT, and this Find is the one place that does not follow it. The intent is therefore already met wherever the note is read. WHAT KEEPS THE FACE RUNG NON-CURRENT ANYWAY is a measurement, not a disagreement with the instruction. Widening this rung to the four current columns (bs_ca__due_from_related_parties_cp, the JV and partnership line, the related-party trade receivable and the trade-and-other aggregate) was tried and measured on the corpus: on China SCE 1966 it published the face's 4,065,231 / 3,914,425 into the LTP column while bs_ca__due_from_related_parties_cp still published the same balance, and the bs_nca__total_non_current_assets reconciliation went from tying EXACTLY (49,227,234 reported against 49,227,234 accounted, and 60,780,612 against 60,780,612) to `mixed_scale` — the one section relation that filing proves, lost. The face prints CP and LTP as two rows and the template rolls them into two different section totals, so a face reading cannot take both without counting one balance twice; a NOTE reading can, because the note is a decomposition and not a section. That is the split the three Finds now record.

cross_check_master.note: The calculated lines whose PRINTED subtotal is read off the filing and compared against the figure the components come to.
